title: Umbrella Santa: swing off a trapeze, open an umbrella, and glide Santa down the right chimney across 15 real towns (free, browser + Android)
author: office-canard
selftext:
Umbrella Santa is a Christmas arcade game. Swing from a trapeze, let go at the right moment, open your umbrella and glide over the snowy rooftops to deliver the present down the chimney with the glowing red stocking. Every delivery is a single shot.



Play in browser: [https://office-canard.itch.io/umbrella-santa-xmas-arcade](https://office-canard.itch.io/umbrella-santa-xmas-arcade)

Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.officecanard.us](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.officecanard.us)



How it started



The trapeze physics came first. In a separate project I was thinking about umbrellas and air resistance, and it felt like the two belonged together. At first the hero was a girl delivering takeout. With the season, she became Santa.



Santa delivers to the whole world, so I wanted the scenery to change as you go. The towns are modeled on real places: Oberndorf, Bruges, Bergen, Prague, Edinburgh, Hallstatt, Zermatt and more. It's Christmas Eve from 3 in the afternoon, and the night deepens one hour per town. I want players to make it to the last one, a big city modeled on New York. Some drama is waiting there.



For the music, I wanted the fun of familiar old carols turning into something else as the arrangement kicks in. Each track opens with a public-domain carol, then the band comes in as acid jazz. Acid, because I didn't want it to be just nostalgic.



How AI fit in



\- Code: Claude wrote it. three.js r128, about 7,700 lines of JS (written with very long lines).

\- Towns: I exported each town from OpenStreetMap. Claude built a tool that turned the buildings, roads, rivers and trees, plus elevation data, into 3D towns, then hand-tuned each town in code: clearing buildings near the course, exaggerating hills, local touches like canal walls and timber framing, a landmark tower per town, and town-specific chimneys.

\- Santa: a Mixamo character recolored as Santa, with Mixamo motions I exported. Claude made the hat and sack in code, wrote the hand-and-arm code that grips the umbrella shaft, and blended the motions. Everything else (umbrella, devices, buildings, chimneys, towers) is built in code.

\- Music: 16 tracks. I set the direction: acid-jazz feel, piano/bass/drums trio, no trumpet, open with the old carol and let the band crash in, big band only for the New York town. Claude composed and arranged all of it, and wrote the old melodies out from memory. Instrument sounds are rendered from the FluidR3 GM soundfont (MIT). Drums are synthesized.

\- Sound effects: two recordings (a party popper from OtoLogic, CC BY 4.0, and a splash from Sound Effect Lab). Everything else, wind, creaks, the umbrella opening, bells, chains, springs and more, is synthesized with Web Audio.

\- Courses: 140 deliveries across 14 towns. I set the rules ("one decision per stage", "it must be reachable by a human hand") and played and gave OK or NG. Claude placed the devices and roofs and built tools to measure them: reach, whether the next target is visible, and the success margin of each link.

\- Testing: Claude brute-forced every input after release with the real physics (896 combinations on stage 1-1), ran a bot that imitates human play to measure success rates, and replayed fixed scenes on all 140 stages after each change. Later I switched to checking by playing it myself.

\- Time: about three weeks, from Nov 4 to Nov 25.



Feedback welcome. I'd love to hear how far you get.
